heading: INT. NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM - TAXIDERMY HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM - TAXIDERMY HALL - NIGHT
A long gallery with a ceiling lost in dark.
Glass cases run down both walls like the windows of a train that stopped decades ago.
Inside them: foxes mid-stride, owls with wings half-raised, a heron balanced on one leg in painted reeds.
Dust lies over everything in a soft grey fur.
Two flashlight beams cross the threshold and wander.
SUNNIVA HALVORSEN (30s, cropped hair, a surveyor's vest with too many pockets) steps in first.
She runs her light across the cases the way a person reads a menu in a language she half knows.
MERIEM AIT-OUDIA (40s, heavy coat, an old camera strapped across her chest) follows two paces behind, breathing through her mouth.
Council wants an inventory by Friday.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: Of what?
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: Everything with a tag.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: Everything here has a tag.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: Sunniva crouches before a case of badgers.
Their glass eyes catch the light and hold it a half-second too long.
She tilts her beam and the shine slides away.
Meriem lifts the camera.
She frames the heron.
She does not press the shutter.
She lowers it, wipes the lens with her sleeve, and lifts it again.
You can take the picture.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: I'm waiting for the light.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: It's a flashlight. It's not going to change.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: Meriem lowers the camera.
She looks at the heron, then at the floor in front of its case.
A line of small, clean prints crosses the dust there, pale and even, as if something had walked the length of the hall on bare feet.
Sunniva sees them a moment after.
She stands.
She sets her light on the floor, pointing along the trail.
It runs to the end of the gallery and into the dark between two cases.
Night guard.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: There is no night guard.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: Then somebody from the cleaning contract.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: No one has cleaned this hall in eleven years.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: The beam trembles.
Neither of them says whose hand is holding it.
Sunniva follows the prints a few steps.
Meriem follows her.
Between the cases there is a narrow service door, painted the same green as the wall.
It is open an inch.
Cold air breathes out of it, smelling of camphor and rain.
Meriem reaches past her and pushes the door wider.
She leans her light into the gap.
Stairs, going down.
On the third stair, a single wet footprint, still shining.
That one's new.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: Yes.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: They stand together at the lip of the stairwell.
Behind them, in the hall, something small and dry settles in one of the cases: a click, like a claw on glass.
Neither turns around.
Sunniva takes out her clipboard.
She writes a line.
She shows it to Meriem.
The page says: BASEMENT - NOT ON INVENTORY.
Meriem nods.
She lifts the camera and, for the first time, presses the shutter.
The flash fills the stairwell white.
In the afterimage, the stairs are exactly as they were.
The wet print is gone.
Friday.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: Friday.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: She pulls the green door shut.
It latches with a sound like a held breath let go.
Both of them go back down the long gallery, past the badgers, past the owls.
They do not hurry.
Behind them, every glass eye in the hall has turned a few degrees toward the door.
Sunniva stops at the exit and puts her hand flat against the wall.
She switches off her light.
Meriem switches off hers.
In the dark, the prints continue to cross the dust, one after another, toward the place where the two women had been standing.
Don't look back.
units.name: SUNNIVA

units.text: I wasn't going to.
units.name: MERIEM

units.text: She opens the door to the street.
Rain falls through the streetlight, ordinary and loud.
They step out into it side by side, and the door swings shut on its own, slow, with the patience of a thing that has all night.
